claims.value: The recovered parent architecture was a historical proposal—not a verified built layout—that replaced a monolithic mega-base with a distributed backbone-and-spurs network: a protected core area, modular low-heat production cells, mining spurs/outposts, power-conducting rails, predominantly single-item lines, and 400-item Storage Depot v.1 or 1,600-item Storage Depot v.2 buffers when unlocked. Rail v.1/v.2/v.3 provide 120/240/480 items per minute, and aggregate trunks were to be upgraded only after measured flow required it.

The 2026-07-11T07:30:00Z controlled delta is an explicit player constraint, not live-game evidence: keep every Base Core at level 0, operate one Constructorizer and two Facturers, preserve Fire Wave protection at every occupied core, exclude hidden/future/pre-Update-1 equipment, and do not construct until the arithmetic is safe. Saved Update 1 production evidence remains authoritative: Constructorizer heat is 500, each Facturer is 650, and a level-0 Base Core has 1,000 capacity; therefore the three machines total 1,800, Constructorizer+Facturer is 1,150 (150 over), two Facturers are 1,300 (300 over), and all three are 1,800 (800 over). Exceeding capacity disables Fire Wave protection.

The safe revised layout is a buildable proposal, not a claim of completed in-save validation: use three occupied level-0 Base Cores, with Core A hosting only the Constructorizer (500 machine heat; at most 500 capacity remains before existing/support load), Core B hosting only Facturer 1 (650; at most 350 remains), and Core C hosting only Facturer 2 (650; at most 350 remains). Reject every heavy-machine co-location. Retain single-item backbone-and-spurs logistics, but because rails conduct power, count every generator, Drone Station, processor, storage unit, defense, and other powered support building at its assigned core and require each projected and observed total to remain strictly below 1,000 after interconnection.

The version-safe next action is to inspect the current Update 1 build/unlock menus and record each candidate Core panel's baseline load, then prepare an itemized per-core heat budget before construction. Use only confirmed Update 1 equipment—Rail v.1/v.2/v.3 are current, while Rail v.4/v.5, hidden-flagged buildings, pre-Update-1 playtest guidance, and unconfirmed level 10–15 Forgotten Engine/endgame content are excluded. Do not rely on Base Core Amplifiers because descriptions say v.1 +50 and v.2 +20 capacity while data fields say -250 and -20. Construct and energize one site at a time only after its total is strictly below 1,000; verify its live Core panel after rail/power connection and stop, isolate, or redesign if attribution is ambiguous or the gate fails.

answer.answer: Committed child checkpoint checkpoint:019f939a-b57c-7753-905c-96ede995b1fe under parent checkpoint:019f9391-da75-7712-8ee2-29b68f0b6050. Retain the distributed backbone-and-spurs plan, but place the 500-heat Constructorizer and each 650-heat Facturer on separate level-0 Base Cores. Their combined 1,800 heat—and every possible pair—exceeds one core's 1,000 capacity. Construction remains gated on verified per-core totals, including all support load, being safely below 1,000.

claims.value: The recovered prior architecture was a proposed, not-yet-built distributed backbone-and-spurs network replacing the superseded monolithic mega-base: powered drone rails carry both items and electricity between a protected core hub, modular low-heat processing cells, and mining spurs/outposts. Use Rail v.1 at 120 items/min initially and upgrade only measured aggregate trunks to Update 1 Rail v.2 at 240 items/min or Rail v.3 at 480 items/min; prefer one item per line, 400-item Storage Depot v.1 handoff buffers when unlocked, and one dedicated one-input Orbital Cargo Launcher per live export product. Defense Turret t1 remains manual-feed; only after Defense Tower t2 is unlocked should it receive a thin Rail v.1 ammunition spur.

The explicit player constraint observed at 2026-07-11T07:30:00Z changes the layout decision—not the authoritative saved production facts—and requires every Base Core to remain level 0, one Constructorizer plus two Facturers to operate, Fire Wave protection at every occupied core, no hidden, future, or pre-Update-1 equipment, and no construction before safe arithmetic. A level-0 core has 1,000 capacity; exceeding it disables Fire Wave protection. Constructorizer heat is 500 and each Facturer is 650, so 500 + 650 + 650 = 1,800. Constructorizer plus Facturer is 1,150, two Facturers are 1,300, and all three are 1,800; every co-location is therefore unsafe before any support-building heat is added.

The safe revised layout is a proposal, not a verified build: use at least three occupied level-0 Base Cores, with the Constructorizer alone on one core at a 500-heat machine baseline and one Facturer alone on each of two other cores at 650-heat baselines. Raw headroom is respectively 500, 350, and 350, but existing buildings, generators, extractors, processors, Drone Stations, storage, and defense support must all be charged to the applicable core. Each complete measured total must remain safely below 1,000; rails may link the three cells and conduct electricity, but they do not combine or relax the separate per-core heat budgets. No pair of required heavy machines may share a level-0 core.

The version-safe next action is to inspect the live Early Access Update 1 0.2.x save and record each candidate Core panel, current load, build/unlock menu, selected recipes, corporation export request, and defense unlocks; then create three complete heat ledgers and begin no construction until all are safely below 1,000. Confirm that Constructorizer, Facturer, required recipes and power, Storage Depot v.1, Orbital Cargo Launcher, and Rail v.1/v.2/v.3 are actually unlocked. Do not use Rail v.4 or v.5, hidden buildings such as Chimeran Power Generator, outdated pre-Update-1 guidance, or level 10–15 endgame/possibly future recipes without live confirmation. Do not credit Base Core Amplifier v.1/v.2 because descriptions claim +50/+20 capacity while data temperature fields show -250/-20; verify in-game first. After the ledgers pass, build one isolated cell at a time and verify measured load and Fire Wave protection after each placement before continuing.

decisions: Reject all co-location among the three required heavy machines at level 0. The minimum safe topology is three occupied cores, one required machine per core; every core's complete measured load, including existing buildings, generators, extraction, processing, storage, and other support, must remain safely below 1,000.

Retain the distributed backbone-and-spurs architecture: rails carry items and electricity; use Rail v.1 at 120 items/min and upgrade only measured aggregate trunks to live Update 1 Rail v.2 at 240 items/min or Rail v.3 at 480 items/min. Prefer one item per line and a 400-item Storage Depot v.1 at important handoffs when unlocked; a dedicated Orbital Cargo Launcher has one input per export product.

Preserve Update 1 authority: the explicit new constraint changes the layout decision but not the saved machine-heat or level-0-capacity facts. Do not use Rail v.4 or v.5, hidden buildings, pre-Update-1 guidance, unconfirmed unlocks, or disputed Base Core Amplifier capacity values as budget credits.

VERIFIED SAVED PRODUCTION FACTS: a level-0 Base Core has 1,000 capacity; exceeding capacity disables Fire Wave protection; Constructorizer heat is 500 and Facturer heat is 650. One Constructorizer plus two Facturers totals 1,800 heat before support buildings.

HISTORICAL/SUPERSEDED: the monolithic mega-base and any same-core pairing of these heavy machines are unsafe at level 0. Constructorizer plus Facturer is 1,150; two Facturers are 1,300; all three are 1,800, each over the 1,000 limit.

PROPOSED, NOT YET BUILT OR VERIFIED IN THE SAVE: use three occupied level-0 Base Cores, assigning the Constructorizer alone to one core at a 500-heat machine baseline and one Facturer alone to each of two other cores at 650-heat machine baselines; raw headroom before existing and support loads is 500, 350, and 350 respectively.
decisions: Reject all co-location among the three required heavy machines at level 0. The minimum safe topology is three occupied cores, one required machine per core; every cores complete measured load, including existing buildings, generators, extraction, processing, storage, and other support, must remain safely below 1,000 rather than consuming the arithmetic headroom.

Retain the distributed backbone-and-spurs architecture: rails carry items and electricity; use Rail v.1 at 120 items/min and upgrade only measured aggregate trunks to live Update 1 Rail v.2 at 240 items/min or Rail v.3 at 480 items/min. Prefer one item per line and a 400-item Storage Depot v.1 at important handoffs when unlocked; a dedicated Orbital Cargo Launcher has one input per export product.

Preserve Update 1 authority: the explicit new constraint changes the layout decision but not the saved machine-heat or level-0-capacity facts. Do not use Rail v.4 or v.5, hidden buildings, pre-Update-1 guidance, unconfirmed unlocks, or disputed Base Core Amplifier capacity values as budget credits.

Construction is gated on a written per-core heat ledger and live Core-panel verification. Build and commission one cell at a time, rechecking measured load and Fire Wave protection before proceeding to the next cell.
next_actions: Record screenshots or notes from each candidate Core panel, the Update 1 build/unlock menus, the selected recipe screens, the corporation export screen, and defense unlocks.

Create three explicit heat ledgers: Constructorizer core = current load + 500 + all support heat; Facturer core B = current load + 650 + all support heat; Facturer core C = current load + 650 + all support heat. Do not place any required machine until every ledger is complete and safely below 1,000.

Once all three ledgers pass, build one isolated heavy-machine cell per core sequentially. After each placement, verify measured Core load and Fire Wave protection before starting the next cell; stop and redesign if any reading differs from the ledger.

Connect the verified cells with only unlocked Rail v.1/v.2/v.3 backbone-and-spur lines, add single-item buffers where unlocked, then measure throughput and queues before upgrading a trunk or adding support heat.

claims.value: RECOVERED PRIOR ARCHITECTURE from parent checkpoint checkpoint:019f9391-da75-7712-8ee2-22b6fa1f4834: a historical proposal, not a verified built state, replacing the monolithic mega-base with a distributed backbone-and-spurs network comprising a protected core hub, low-heat processing cells, and mining spurs/outposts. Rails conduct electricity; begin with Rail v.1 at 120 items/min and upgrade aggregate trunks to Update 1 Rail v.2 or v.3 at 240 or 480 items/min only when measured flow requires it, while preserving substantial margin below each level-0 Base Core capacity of 1,000.

CURRENT SUPERSEDING PLAYER CONSTRAINT, observed 2026-07-11T07:30:00Z: operate one Constructorizer and two Facturers while every Base Core remains level 0, preserve Fire Wave protection at every occupied core, exclude hidden, future, and pre-Update-1 equipment, and do not start construction until the arithmetic is safe; saved production evidence remains authoritative for heat and capacity. A Constructorizer is 500 heat, each Facturer is 650, and total heavy-machine heat is 500+(2x650)=1,800. Against a level-0 capacity of 1,000, Constructorizer+Facturer is 1,150, or 150 over; two Facturers are 1,300, or 300 over; and all three are 1,800, or 800 over. Every such co-location is rejected because exceeding capacity disables Fire Wave protection.

SAFE REVISED PROPOSAL, not yet built or verified: use three distinct occupied level-0 Base Cores on the distributed backbone-and-spurs network. Assign one Constructorizer to Core A for 500/1,000 heat with at most 500 additional local heat, one Facturer to Core B for 650/1,000 with at most 350 additional heat, and the second Facturer to Core C for 650/1,000 with at most 350 additional heat. These local margins are non-transferable: each core must independently include its existing load and every supporting extractor, processor, generator, storage, drone, and defense load and remain at or below 1,000; otherwise support load must move to another level-0 core or construction must be postponed.

VERSION-SAFE NEXT ACTION: before construction, inspect each candidate Core panel and the live Update 1 build/unlock menu, inventory baseline and support-building heat, and confirm the Constructorizer, Facturer, recipes, and selected Rail v.1/v.2/v.3 components are actually available. Exclude Rail v.4/v.5, hidden or future content, and pre-Update-1 guidance; starrupture.tools data may mix unavailable content, while original Creepy Jar Update 1 patch authority governs actual availability. Do not credit Base Core Amplifier v.1 or v.2 because their descriptions and temperature fields conflict. Build one dedicated cell at a time only after all three projected totals are at most 1,000, verifying the Core panel and Fire Wave protection after every placement.

answer.answer: Persisted child checkpoint checkpoint:019f9399-1683-73c2-9d5e-14b80b3c537e with parent checkpoint:019f9391da887de1a7a2bc4f60399133 retained. The safe proposal uses three separate level-0 Base Cores: one 500-heat Constructorizer and one 650-heat Facturer at each of two other cores. claims.value: The recovered prior architecture is a proposed, not-yet-built distributed backbone-and-spurs network rather than the superseded monolithic mega-base: rails distribute both items and power among a protected core hub, low-heat processing cells, and mining spurs/outposts; use Rail v.1 initially, upgrade aggregate trunks to Update 1 Rail v.2/v.3 only when measured flow exceeds 120/240 items per minute, and prefer one item per line with single-item buffers.

The superseding explicit player constraint, observed 2026-07-11T07:30:00Z, requires every Base Core to remain level 0, operation of one Constructorizer plus two Facturers, Fire Wave protection at every occupied core, no hidden/future/pre-Update-1 equipment, and safe heat arithmetic before construction. Saved production facts remain authoritative: level-0 capacity is 1,000, exceeding it disables Fire Wave protection, Constructorizer heat is 500, and each Facturer is 650; required heavy-machine heat is 500 + 650 + 650 = 1,800.

The safe revised layout is a proposal—not a verified build—using three separate, non-overlapping occupied level-0 Base Cores: the Constructorizer alone at one core and one Facturer alone at each of two other cores, connected only with confirmed Update 1 logistics. The Constructorizer core may have at most 500 measured existing-plus-support heat before its 500-heat machine is added, and each Facturer core may have at most 350 before adding its 650-heat machine. Reject Constructorizer-plus-Facturer co-location at 1,150, two-Facturer co-location at 1,300, and all-three co-location at 1,800 because each exceeds 1,000; do not rely on disputed Amplifier values.

Before construction, record each candidate core's actual load and the live Update 1 unlock menus, count every planned local support building, and proceed only when the Constructorizer site's pre-machine load is at most 500 and each Facturer site's is at most 350. Then build one site at a time and recheck total load and Fire Wave protection after every placement, stopping if any core would exceed 1,000. Use only actually unlocked Update 1 equipment—Rail v.1/v.2/v.3 are current at 120/240/480 items per minute; Rail v.4/v.5, hidden equipment, pre-Update-1 information, level-10–15 endgame/possibly-future recipes, and unverified Amplifier capacity must not authorize the build.

gates.title: Every occupied Base Core remains level 0 and its measured total load, including the assigned heavy machine and all local support buildings, is at or below the authoritative 1,000 capacity before construction proceeds.

The Constructorizer site has no more than 500 measured existing-plus-support heat before adding its 500-heat Constructorizer; each Facturer site has no more than 350 measured existing-plus-support heat before adding its 650-heat Facturer.

No Constructorizer is co-located with a Facturer (500 + 650 = 1,150), no two Facturers are co-located (650 + 650 = 1,300), and all three are never co-located (500 + 650 + 650 = 1,800), because each combination exceeds a level-0 core's 1,000 capacity.

Only equipment confirmed for Early Access Update 1 is used; do not depend on Rail v.4/v.5, hidden or pre-Update-1 equipment, level-10–15 endgame/possibly-future recipes, or unverified Base Core Amplifier capacity values.
After each heavy-machine placement, re-read that core's measured load and stop before placing the next machine unless Fire Wave protection remains enabled and total load is at or below 1,000.

goals.title: Revise the resumed distributed Update 1 factory plan into a buildable level-0 design for one Constructorizer plus two Facturers while preserving Fire Wave protection at every occupied core.

next_actions.title: Before construction, inspect and record the Core panel and current load at each of three candidate non-overlapping level-0 sites, plus the live Update 1 build/unlock menus.

Prepare three site budgets from measured values: Constructorizer site existing-plus-support heat must be at most 500; each Facturer site existing-plus-support heat must be at most 350. Relocate optional support or choose another level-0 core if a budget fails; do not use an amplifier to paper over the discrepancy.

After all three budgets pass, build sequentially: place the 500-heat Constructorizer at its dedicated core and recheck total load/Fire Wave protection; then place each 650-heat Facturer at its own dedicated core, rechecking after each. Stop immediately if any occupied core would exceed 1,000.

Connect the three cells with only actually unlocked Update 1 logistics, keeping flows on one-item lines and matching Rail v.1/v.2/v.3 capacity to measured rates; validate queues and line rates before any trunk upgrade.

current_state: CURRENT REQUIREMENT (explicit player constraint, observed 2026-07-11T07:30:00Z): keep every Base Core at level 0, operate one Constructorizer and two Facturers, preserve Fire Wave protection at every occupied core, use no hidden/future/pre-Update-1 equipment, and do not begin construction until heat arithmetic is safe. The requirement changes layout, not the saved production facts.

RECOVERED PRIOR STATE: the parent checkpoint replaced the monolithic mega-base with a proposed, not-yet-built distributed backbone-and-spurs network: protected core hub, low-heat processing cells, mining spurs/outposts, Rail v.1 initially, v.2/v.3 only when measured aggregation requires, and one item per rail line with single-item buffers.

AUTHORITATIVE HEAT FACTS: a level-0 Base Core has 1,000 capacity and exceeding capacity disables Fire Wave protection; Constructorizer heat is 500 and each Facturer heat is 650. Required heavy-machine heat is 500 + 650 + 650 = 1,800 in aggregate.

SAFE REVISED PROPOSAL, NOT YET BUILT OR VERIFIED IN THE SAVE: use three separate, non-overlapping occupied level-0 core sites, assigning the Constructorizer alone to one core and one Facturer alone to each of the other two. This leaves at most 500 heat for measured existing/support load at the Constructorizer core and 350 at each Facturer core.
decisions: Reject all heavy-machine co-location at level 0: Constructorizer + Facturer is 1,150 heat, two Facturers are 1,300 heat, and all three are 1,800 heat, each above the 1,000 capacity.
Do not rely on Base Core Amplifiers because the saved descriptions and temperature fields conflict; the three-core layout must pass against the unamplified 1,000 capacity at every level-0 core.

Retain the Update 1 distributed logistics authority: rails conduct power; use confirmed Rail v.1/v.2/v.3 at 120/240/480 items per minute and upgrade aggregation trunks only from measured need. Exclude Rail v.4/v.5 and hidden/future/pre-Update-1 equipment.

Treat 500 and 350 as maximum per-site budgets for all existing and support heat before placing the corresponding heavy machine, not as automatically available headroom. A site is buildable only after its actual load and every planned local support building are counted.
next_actions: Before construction, inspect and record the Core panel and current load at each of three candidate non-overlapping level-0 sites, plus the live Update 1 build/unlock menus.

Prepare three site budgets from measured values: Constructorizer site existing-plus-support heat must be at most 500; each Facturer site existing-plus-support heat must be at most 350. Relocate optional support or choose another level-0 core if a budget fails; do not use an amplifier to paper over the discrepancy.

After all three budgets pass, build sequentially: place the 500-heat Constructorizer at its dedicated core and recheck total load/Fire Wave protection; then place each 650-heat Facturer at its own dedicated core, rechecking after each. Stop immediately if any occupied core would exceed 1,000.

Connect the three cells with only actually unlocked Update 1 logistics, keeping flows on one-item lines and matching Rail v.1/v.2/v.3 capacity to measured rates; validate queues and line rates before any trunk upgrade.

answer.answer: Reopened parent checkpoint checkpoint:019f9391-f6d6-7782-85fe-efb9b5509543, applied the revision-N+1 API-gate delta, and committed child checkpoint checkpoint:019f939a-9f84-70e1-be0b-3c06ab8cecad in four CarryState calls. The historical token result is now correctly bounded as retrieval-only evidence, and the checkpoint defines the first persistent build slice plus an explicit, not-yet-verified transition gate.

claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable, agent-first context and durable-work layer whose product purpose is durable machine continuity: it preserves learned knowledge and live resumable state—including goals, evidence, decisions, hypotheses, plans, artifacts, computations, unresolved questions, rejected paths, checkpoints, and next safe actions—so later agents can inspect, revise, advance, verify, and hand off work. It is not primarily a notes app, wiki, transcript archive, synchronized folder, retrieval system, or memory database; Obsidian and Markdown are prototype corpora, human projections, and export formats rather than the canonical product boundary.

The verified 2026-07-10 retrieval-only result was: policy 0.2 Memory Workspace passed 17/20 cases, recovered 46/53 evidence items, held P95 context to 11,999 characters, and used about 2,932 mean estimated tokens; one-shot BM25 top-k also passed 17/20, recovered 48/53, and used about 1,070 mean estimated tokens. The correct interpretation is that this narrow benchmark did not demonstrate the workspace hypothesis and made policy 0.2 and BM25 regression baselines; the tuned result was not holdout evidence, and the lower top-k token figure does not establish BM25 as the product architecture or disprove a durable workspace. Correctness, evidence-chain recall, temporal and contradiction handling, source fidelity, and successful continuation outrank latency and cost. Superseding project-owner direction observed at 2026-07-11T08:00:00Z therefore advances implementation to a persistent workspace and requires cumulative cached replay and uncached input to be reported separately.

The authoritative first implementation slice—still implementation work, not a completed result—is a persistent, snapshot-pinned workspace replacing the process-per-operation BM25 shell as the target architecture. It must reopen a parent checkpoint created at corpus revision N; refresh into N+1 and expose changed evidence or constraints as a diff; combine exact and lexical retrieval with a pluggable semantic path; batch query and read operations through a typed API; commit an immutable child checkpoint that names its parent and preserves source references; and avoid reconstructing the complete prior corpus when checkpoint plus delta are sufficient. The BM25 shell remains a regression fixture.

The measurable transition gate is no more than four completed workspace calls per case while matching the direct-filesystem answer claims, with cumulative cached replay and uncached input reported separately. Functional acceptance also requires revision-N parent reopening, visible N-to-N+1 diff, typed batched query/read behavior, immutable parent-linked child creation, and preservation of both prior and delta source references without full-corpus reconstruction. This handoff used exactly four calls and committed the parent-linked child checkpoint, but implementation-harness claim parity and accounting remain unverified work rather than a claimed pass.

HISTORICAL VERIFIED RESULT: In the 2026-07-10 retrieval-only benchmark, policy 0.2 Memory Workspace and one-shot BM25 top-k each passed 17 of 20 cases; the workspace recovered 46 of 53 evidence items with P95 context of 11,999 characters and about 2,932 mean estimated tokens, while one-shot top-k recovered 48 of 53 and used about 1,070 mean estimated tokens. That result did not demonstrate the workspace hypothesis, froze policy 0.2 as a regression baseline, and was not holdout evidence.

SUPERSEDING CURRENT DIRECTION: Explicit project-owner direction observed at 2026-07-11T08:00:00Z authorizes implementation of a persistent, snapshot-pinned workspace; the process-per-operation BM25 shell remains a regression fixture, not the target architecture.
decisions: Correct the token interpretation: the historical about 1,070 versus 2,932 figures are mean estimated tokens from a narrow retrieval-only comparison, not proof that BM25 is the product architecture or that a durable workspace failed as a product; correctness, complete evidence-chain recall, temporal and contradiction handling, source fidelity, and successful continuation outrank latency and cost, and the new harness must report cumulative cached replay separately from uncached input.

Define the first persistent build slice as a typed API workflow that reopens a parent checkpoint at corpus revision N, refreshes into N+1 with the changed evidence or constraint exposed as a diff, combines exact and lexical retrieval with a pluggable semantic path, batches query and read operations, commits an immutable source-preserving child checkpoint naming its parent, and avoids reconstructing the complete prior corpus when checkpoint plus delta are sufficient.

Set the transition acceptance gate at no more than four completed workspace calls per case while matching the direct-filesystem answer claims, with cumulative cached replay and uncached input reported separately.
Do not reopen settled product framing during this slice, and do not treat canonical storage, schema, deployment, semantic backend, or commercial architecture as selected by the transition decision.

answer.answer: Straylight now advances from a retrieval-only evaluation into an authorized persistent-workspace implementation slice. The historical token result favored one-shot BM25 within that narrow benchmark; it did not establish product success or disprove the durable-work thesis. Child checkpoint checkpoint:019f939a-acc4-7ea1-8322-35677de1cfad was committed with its parent and prior-plus-delta source lineage. Implementation acceptance requires claim parity with direct-filesystem answers in no more than four completed workspace calls per case, with cached replay and uncached input reported separately.

claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable, agent-first context and durable-work layer: it preserves learned knowledge together with resumable live work state—including evidence, decisions, hypotheses, plans, artifacts, computations, unresolved questions, rejected paths, checkpoints, and the next safe action—so later agents can inspect, revise, advance, verify, and hand off complex work. It is not primarily a notes app, wiki, synchronized folder, transcript archive, retrieval product, or memory database; Obsidian and Markdown are prototype inputs, human projections, and export formats rather than the canonical product boundary.

The historical 2026-07-10 retrieval-only benchmark contained 20 frozen questions and 53 gold evidence items. The initial workspace passed 12/20 cases; one policy-only tuning pass, without changing the manifest or corpus, produced policy 0.2 at 17/20 cases, 46/53 evidence items, and 11,999 characters P95 context. One-shot BM25 top-k also passed 17/20, recovered 48/53, and used about 1,070 mean estimated tokens versus 2,932 for the workspace. The correct interpretation is that one-shot top-k was the strongest default for that retrieval benchmark and the workspace hypothesis was not demonstrated there; policy 0.2 is a frozen regression baseline whose tuned score is not holdout evidence. Retrieval-only performance is not the product acceptance result, direct source access remains an escalation path, and the process-per-operation BM25 shell is now a regression fixture rather than the target architecture.

The first persistent build slice is an explicit project-owner implementation decision observed at 2026-07-11T08:00:00Z in source version sha256:dd4acbe1bfad4be3983422ebee7e73239b66486e1ffbe199bb760d5d5b6ba2e9: replace the process-per-operation BM25 target with a persistent, snapshot-pinned workspace that reopens a parent checkpoint created at corpus revision N; refreshes to N+1 and exposes changed evidence or constraints as a diff; combines exact and lexical retrieval with a pluggable semantic path; batches query and read operations through a typed API; commits an immutable child naming its parent and preserving source references; and avoids reconstructing the complete prior corpus when the checkpoint and delta suffice. This is the authorized implementation slice, not a verified completed implementation.

The measurable transition gate is an acceptance target, not a completed result: every transition-harness case must finish in no more than four completed workspace calls while matching the direct-filesystem answer claims, and reporting must separate cumulative cached replay from uncached input. Each accepted case must also exercise the N-to-N+1 diff and produce an immutable child checkpoint with parent and source lineage under the first-slice requirements.

answer.answer: Straylight has advanced from its retrieval-only evaluation into the authorized persistent-API implementation phase. The historical token comparison is retained only as regression-baseline evidence, and child checkpoint checkpoint:019f939a-6aaf-7c23-bf60-8c38e999eef1 now records the first build slice, measurable four-call transition gate, parent lineage, and source references.

claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable context and durable-work layer for Codex, Claude Code, personal laptop agents, OpenClaw/Hermes-style systems, and future agent runtimes. It must preserve learned knowledge and live resumable work state—including evidence, decisions, hypotheses, plans, artifacts, computations, unresolved questions, rejected paths, checkpoints, and the next safe action—so a later agent can inspect provenance, resume and revise complex work, and leave improved durable state; Obsidian and Markdown are prototype inputs, human projections, and exports rather than the canonical product boundary.

The verified retrieval-only result was that tuned policy 0.2 passed 17 of 20 cases and recovered 46 of 53 evidence items at P95 context of 11,999 characters, while one-shot BM25 top-k also passed 17 of 20, recovered 48 of 53, and used about 1,070 mean estimated tokens versus 2,932 for the minimal stateful workspace. This did not demonstrate the workspace hypothesis: policy 0.2 was tuned rather than holdout evidence, one-shot top-k remained the strongest retrieval default, and the process-per-operation BM25 shell is now only a regression fixture. The 1,070-versus-2,932 result must therefore not be interpreted as the cost or verdict for the target persistent API; future results must report cumulative cached replay separately from uncached input.

The first persistent build slice is a snapshot-pinned typed workspace API that reopens a parent checkpoint created at corpus revision N, refreshes into revision N+1, exposes changed evidence or constraints as a diff, combines exact and lexical retrieval with a pluggable semantic path, batches query and read operations, and commits an immutable child checkpoint naming its parent and preserving source references. When checkpoint plus delta are sufficient, it must avoid reconstructing the complete prior corpus.

The measurable transition gate requires each harness case to satisfy the complete revision-N-to-N+1 workflow in no more than four completed workspace calls while matching the direct-filesystem answer claims; it must separately report cumulative cached replay and uncached input, demonstrate exact plus lexical retrieval with a pluggable semantic path through batched typed operations, preserve the parent and source lineage in an immutable child checkpoint, and avoid full prior-corpus reconstruction when checkpoint plus delta suffice.

answer.answer: Straylight has advanced into implementation under the persistent API gate. The historical token figures remain retrieval-only efficiency measurements, not evidence that the workspace hypothesis or target architecture succeeded. The required first slice is a persistent, snapshot-pinned typed workspace, and checkpoint:019f939b-28f5-7ba3-a296-8e77bea4d4e2 was committed as a child of checkpoint:019f9391-f6f5-7343-befa-9a967f1fcd4b with prior and delta source lineage.

claims.value: Straylight, distinct from the Metis knowledge-base system, is an agent-first portable context and durable-work product and protocol—not primarily a notes app, wiki, transcript archive, synchronized folder, retrieval system, or memory database. It preserves durable knowledge plus the live state needed to resume and advance work: goals, evidence, decisions, hypotheses, plans, artifacts, computations, unresolved questions, rejected paths, checkpoints, and next actions. Memory must be user-owned, portable, inspectable, reversible, provenance-bearing, and freshness-aware; Obsidian and Markdown are prototype corpora, human projections, and export formats, while full source artifacts and evidence remain available as the truth boundary.

The historical retrieval-only evaluation initially produced 12/20 workspace passes; after one policy-level tuning pass without changing the manifest or corpus, policy 0.2 produced 17/20 cases and 46/53 evidence items with P95 context of 11,999 characters. One-shot BM25 top-k produced 17/20 cases and 48/53 evidence items using about 1,070 mean estimated tokens versus 2,932 for the workspace. These figures show that one-shot top-k was the stronger default in that run and that the workspace hypothesis was not demonstrated; policy 0.2 is a tuned regression baseline, not untouched-holdout or product-success evidence. The token comparison must not be interpreted as validation of the persistent target architecture, and the new transition evaluation must report cumulative cached replay separately from uncached input.

The required first persistent build slice is not yet verified as implemented. It must replace the process-per-operation BM25 shell target with a persistent, snapshot-pinned workspace that reopens a parent checkpoint created at corpus revision N; explicitly refreshes into N+1 and exposes changed evidence or constraints as a diff; combines exact and lexical retrieval with a pluggable semantic path; batches query and read operations through a typed API; commits an immutable child checkpoint naming its parent and preserving source references; and avoids reconstructing the complete prior corpus when the checkpoint and delta suffice. The BM25 shell remains only a regression fixture.

The measurable transition gate accepts the persistent slice only when every harness case completes in no more than four workspace calls while its answer claims match the direct-filesystem answer claims, with cumulative cached replay and uncached input reported separately. Functional acceptance also requires the revision-N-to-N+1 diff, typed batched query/read, exact-plus-lexical retrieval with a pluggable semantic path, and an immutable child checkpoint that preserves parent and source lineage without unnecessary full-corpus reconstruction.

CURRENT FACT: Straylight is an agent-first, user-owned, portable, inspectable, reversible, provenance-bearing, freshness-aware context and durable-work layer that preserves durable knowledge plus live resumable work state; full source evidence remains authoritative while summaries, embeddings, indexes, and context packs are derived aids.

HISTORICAL VERIFIED RETRIEVAL-ONLY RESULT: Policy 0.2 scored 17/20 cases and 46/53 evidence items at P95 context 11,999 characters; one-shot BM25 top-k scored 17/20 and 48/53 at about 1,070 mean estimated tokens versus 2,932 for the workspace. That result did not demonstrate the workspace hypothesis, policy 0.2 was tuned rather than untouched-holdout evidence, and the scores remain a regression baseline rather than the product gate.
INCOMPLETE WORK: No persistent snapshot-pinned implementation or completed transition-harness result is evidenced yet.
decisions: Interpret the historical token figures only as retrieval-run efficiency measurements: do not infer product success or architecture superiority from them; the new transition harness must report cumulative cached replay and uncached input separately.
Build a persistent, snapshot-pinned workspace rather than the process-per-operation BM25 shell prototype; keep that shell only as a regression fixture.

The first persistent slice must reopen a revision-N parent checkpoint, explicitly refresh to N+1 with an evidence/constraint diff, combine exact and lexical retrieval with a pluggable semantic path, batch typed query/read operations, commit an immutable child naming its parent and preserving source references, and avoid full-corpus reconstruction when checkpoint plus delta suffice.
open_questions: Which semantic retrieval implementation should back the pluggable path in the first slice?
What minimal typed request, response, checkpoint, diff, and evidence-envelope schema should be frozen for the transition harness without prematurely settling the canonical storage architecture?
next_actions: Implement persistent session open/refresh so a checkpoint pinned at revision N can refresh explicitly to N+1 and return the changed evidence or constraint as a diff.
Implement typed batched query/read with exact and lexical retrieval plus a pluggable semantic path.
Implement immutable child-checkpoint commit with parent lineage and preserved source references, using checkpoint plus delta without reconstructing the full prior corpus.

Run the transition harness and accept the slice only when every case completes in no more than four workspace calls, its answer claims match the direct-filesystem answer claims, and cumulative cached replay and uncached input are reported separately.

checkpoints.title: Advance Straylight from evaluation into implementation by delivering the first persistent, snapshot-pinned typed workspace slice and proving it against the API transition harness.

answer.answer: Committed child checkpoint checkpoint:019f939b-8b47-7251-a9b8-8846cb2af98e, retaining parent checkpoint:019f9391-f6e8-7421-b552-8076aa554f96 and prior-plus-delta source lineage. Straylight now moves from its retrieval-only evaluation into a persistent, snapshot-pinned API slice with a measurable four-call transition gate.

claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable, agent-first context and durable-work layer. It preserves learned knowledge and live resumable work state—including evidence, decisions, hypotheses, plans, artifacts, computations, unresolved questions, rejected paths, checkpoints, and the next safe action—so later agents can inspect provenance, revise work as evidence changes, and leave improved durable state. It is not primarily a notes app, wiki, synchronized folder, transcript archive, retrieval product, or memory database; Obsidian and Markdown are prototype inputs, human projections, and export formats rather than the canonical product boundary.

The historical retrieval-only result was that policy 0.2's workspace passed 17 of 20 cases, recovered 46 of 53 evidence items, and held P95 context to 11,999 characters, while one-shot top-k also passed 17 of 20, recovered 48 of 53, and used about 1,070 mean estimated tokens versus 2,932 for the workspace. This did not demonstrate the workspace hypothesis: policy 0.2 is a regression baseline, its tuned score is not holdout evidence, and the token comparison is an efficiency measurement rather than proof of product success or authority for the target architecture. Under the superseding owner direction observed at 2026-07-11T08:00:00Z, the process-per-operation BM25 shell remains only a regression fixture, and transition reporting must distinguish cumulative cached replay from uncached input.

The owner-directed first persistent build slice is a persistent, snapshot-pinned typed workspace API that reopens a parent checkpoint created at corpus revision N; explicitly refreshes to N+1 and returns the changed evidence or constraint as a diff; combines exact and lexical retrieval with a pluggable semantic path; batches query and read operations; commits an immutable child checkpoint naming its parent and preserving source references; and avoids reconstructing the complete prior corpus when the checkpoint and delta suffice.

The prospective transition gate passes only when each harness case completes in no more than four workspace calls and matches the direct-filesystem answer claims, while cumulative cached replay and uncached input are reported separately. The case must also demonstrate the N-to-N+1 diff, exact and lexical retrieval with a pluggable semantic path, typed batched query/read, immutable parent-linked checkpoint lineage with preserved source references, and no unnecessary full-corpus reconstruction; the source establishes these acceptance criteria, not a completed implementation result.

current_state: CURRENT FACT: Straylight is a user-owned, portable, agent-first context and durable-work layer that preserves learned knowledge and live resumable work state with provenance, corrections, freshness, and full source/artifact access.

HISTORICAL VERIFIED RESULT: Retrieval policy 0.2 and one-shot top-k each passed 17 of 20 retrieval cases; the workspace recovered 46 of 53 evidence items with P95 context of 11,999 characters, while one-shot recovered 48 of 53 and used about 1,070 mean estimated tokens versus 2,932 for the workspace. That result did not demonstrate the workspace hypothesis and is now a regression baseline, not the product acceptance decision.

SUPERSEDING OWNER DIRECTION observed at 2026-07-11T08:00:00Z: proceed from evaluation into implementation using a persistent, snapshot-pinned workspace; the process-per-operation BM25 shell remains only a regression fixture.
INCOMPLETE WORK: The persistent implementation slice and its transition harness are now defined but are not evidenced as built or passed.
decisions: Interpret the historical token comparison as a retrieval-only efficiency result, not proof of product success or a reason to keep the BM25 shell as the target architecture; correctness, continuation, durable-state quality, and source fidelity remain primary.

The first persistent build slice is a snapshot-pinned typed workspace API that reopens checkpoint N, refreshes to N+1 with a diff, combines exact and lexical retrieval with a pluggable semantic path, batches query/read, and commits an immutable lineage-preserving child without full-corpus reconstruction when checkpoint plus delta suffice.
Measure token use by separately reporting cumulative cached replay and uncached input.

Implement typed batched query/read over exact and lexical retrieval with a pluggable semantic backend.
Implement immutable child-checkpoint commit with explicit parent linkage and preserved evidence/source references.
Run the transition harness against direct-filesystem controls; record per-case call count, answer-claim parity, cumulative cached replay, and uncached input.
